the question of how working memory capacity is limited, and how this limitation is reflected in performance on memory span tasks.

the cognitive mechanisms that support the performance of adults on the most widely used working memory tasks.

the time-based resource sharing model accounts for working memory capacity in adults.

we are trying to explain why people have trouble remembering things.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the cognitive load of a working memory task depends on the number of items to be maintained and the time available for processing and maintenance.
the cognitive load of a task depends not only on the number of processes that are required to perform it but also on the time available to perform them.
the cognitive load of a task can be measured in terms of a number of retrievals to perform:time to perform them ratio, which determines the time constraints on the task.
